faros-headline [headline; frozen page excerpt]: For every code change merged, the probability of a production incident has more than tripled.

faros-ratio [measurement; frozen page excerpt]: The incidents-to-PR ratio is up 242.7% as teams move from low to high AI adoption.

faros-not-probability [qualification; frozen page excerpt]: This is a ratio, not a probability: a single PR can be linked to multiple incidents, and not every incident traces directly to the most recent merge.

faros-method [qualification; frozen page excerpt]: It is a measurement of what AI is actually producing across the full software development lifecycle, tracking metric change between periods of lowest and highest AI adoption within each organization.

faros-observational [qualification; authored context]: The period comparison is observational. It is not a randomized causal effect, and it does not show that AI caused the change.

faros-population [qualification; frozen page excerpt]: The AI Engineering Impact Report 2026: The Acceleration Whiplash draws on two years of telemetry data from 22,000 developers and more than 4,000 teams across the Faros platform, tracking metric change between each organization's periods of lowest and highest AI adoption.

faros-no-randomized-effect [gap; authored context]: The frozen takeaway page does not report a randomized effect.

faros-report-not-captured [gap; authored context]: The full report was not captured; this brief is limited to the frozen takeaway page.

faros-monthly [measurement; frozen page excerpt]: Monthly incidents are up 57.9%.
